paragraphs.text: Palagano et al. (2018) studied an Indian family with 2 affected sibs. Exome sequencing found a novel homozygous truncating mutation in the NBAS gene in both patients. Two cellular processes linked to NBAS, nonsense-mediated decay and Golgi-to-endoplasmic reticulum retrograde traffic, were impaired in HEK293T cells overexpressing the truncated NBAS protein. The authors tested this by real-time PCR, Western blot analysis, coimmunoprecipitation, and immunofluorescence. In mouse embryos at various developmental stages, immunohistochemistry showed NBAS expression in developing chondrogenic and osteogenic structures of the skeleton and in the cortex, hippocampus, and cerebellum.

agent.process_note: I read both files in full. For Prontera et al. (2011) only the title was available (two sisters of Indian origin with AFFND1). For Palagano et al. (2018) only the abstract was available. It gives a homozygous truncating NBAS mutation in an Indian family with 2 affected sibs, plus functional, mouse and zebrafish data. The abstract does not give the nucleotide or protein change, so I could not write an allelic variant entry. It also does not report consanguinity, segregation details or clinical specifics. Neither paper says whether the two reports describe the same family, so I did not link them. No HGNC reference data were supplied, so the intro leaves out the NBAS MIM number and chromosomal location.
